name: Native and pinned reference request comparison R1
order: Alternate native/reference then reference/native per block. Rotate workload order by block, identically for both backends.
sampling: Sample Swift/Python frontend and helper physical footprint via proc_pid_rusage every 0.2 seconds. Record process sums and individual peaks; do not call RSS a physical footprint.
timing: Complete in-process request includes template/tokenizer, grammar preparation, generation, streaming projection and terminal validation. Startup separately includes frontend initialization and helper readiness; coordinator also reports process-launch-to-ready. OS file caches are uncontrolled, so this is process-cold, not SSD-cold.
equality: Require identical prompt token IDs, generation-prefix counts, request parameters and exact declared semantic outputs in each paired request. Retain generated token differences and output length. Universal byte-for-byte generation equivalence is not assumed.
conditions: No overlapping model jobs, builds or downloads. Hold the shared inference lease across each comparison. Require AC power and record thermal, memory-pressure, swap and load before and after each worker block. Retain every attempted block.
exclusions: Exclude the entire paired block only for lost AC power, serious/critical thermal pressure, or verified external overlapping inference. Record reason and both raw outputs. Swap growth is a finding, not grounds to discard an inconvenient result. A failed or mismatched request fails the gate; do not drop it.
pilot: One block with one repetition per workload exercises the harness only. Pilot results cannot satisfy adoption or speed claims. Repairs must retain failed pilot outputs and precede the qualifying run.
limits: This isolates matched request/frontend behavior. Actual workbook-job timing, full UI, long-context and hardware gates remain separate. Removing Python does not establish a speedup. Twenty samples per workload give an observed p95, not a population-tail guarantee.
